en: The Sutra of the Secret Treasury of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva’s Wish-Fulfilling Wheel Dhāraṇī Divine Spell,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan during the Tang Dynasty.
Chapter One: The Dhāraṇī for Eliminating All Evil Karma. Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Buddha was staying on Mount Kāliṅga.
Together with a great assembly of bodhisattvas,
at that time the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara rose from his seat and adjusted his robes.
Kneeling with palms joined, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I possess a great dhāraṇī method named the Mahāpadma-candana-maṇi-hṛdaya-cakra."
One will be able to achieve success in all matters sought after.
If the Tathāgata, out of great compassion, permits me to speak,
I shall rely upon the Buddha’s spiritual power.
It is spoken for the benefit of all sentient beings.
Why is this? World-Honored One, this dhāraṇī...
Possessing great supernatural power like a maṇi jewel,
and like a wish-fulfilling tree capable of satisfying all aspirations,
the World-Honored One then praised the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
Excellent, excellent! Because you possess compassion, you have been able to ask such questions for the sake of sentient beings.
Listen without obstruction.
Having spoken this dhāraṇī,
the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, having received permission,
rose, joined his palms in prostration, and returned to his original seat.
Observing that the assembly was present and possessed great compassion,
he then spoke this mantra:

*Namo ratnatrayāya | Namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ cakravadhi-candana-maṇi mahāpātme lulu tiṣṭha cavarāgra hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.* The above is the body-mantra (*kāyavidyā*).
Oṃ padume candanamanisamaya mahācavara hūṃ. The above is the heart-mantra.
Oṃ varada padume hūṃ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara...
When this *Cintāmaṇicakra-dhāraṇī* had been spoken,
the great earth shook in six ways;
the palaces of the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and so forth, all trembled.
The Māra King and all the māra-beings were struck with great terror;
fire broke out in all the palaces of the Māra King,
as did that of the other species of yakṣas and malevolent spirits.
They were all struck with terror and fell prostrate upon the ground.
All the gates of hell opened,
and the sinners were liberated to receive the supreme bliss of the heavens.
At that time, celestial rain fell of precious flowers and various kinds of precious ornaments;
the music of the devas resounded in the void,
producing diverse sounds as an offering to the Tathāgata.
At that time, the World-Honored One, with a Brahma-like voice, spoke in verse to praise the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
“Excellent, excellent! You, O son of good family, who out of compassion for sentient beings...”
I shall proclaim this dhāraṇī, which can cause all sentient beings to attain great and supreme benefit.
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"O son of good family, for the sake of all sentient beings..."
When this Dharma of the Great Sovereign Dhāraṇī of Divine Power was being taught,
the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Buddha, saying:
"If there be good sons or good daughters, bhikṣus or bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas or upāsikās, or boys or girls..."
If, within this life, one desires to seek immediate retribution,
one should, throughout day and night, apply oneself with single-minded diligence and not forget this dhāraṇī.
Furthermore, one need not discriminate between auspicious or inauspicious days;
once the recitation is mastered, its efficacy will immediately manifest.
For whatever matter one seeks, one should recite it one hundred and eight times.
Thus, hundreds of thousands of matters are accomplished;
there is no other divine mantra or dhāraṇī superior to this King of Wish-Fulfilling Wheels (Cintāmaṇicakra-rāja-dhāraṇī). Why is this so?
It can completely destroy the heavy obstacles of evil karma from the past and present.
If one is able to recite this dhāraṇī,
even those destined for the Avīci Hell shall immediately attain liberation.
Even the five heinous crimes and other such offenses will all be completely eradicated;
how much more so other evil karmas,
as well as all calamities and illnesses?
Whether it be fevers lasting one, two, three, or four days;
whether occurring by day or by night; or diseases such as those caused by wind, bile, phlegm, or mucus—the reciter of this mantra shall find them all completely cured.
If one is afflicted by *gū* poison, malevolent incantations,
carbuncles, scabies, leprosy, itching, insanity, headaches,
or ailments of the ears, nose, lips, tongue, teeth, or throat;
Pains in the mouth, face, head, brain, chest, ribs, heart, abdomen,
waist, back, hands, feet, and toes are all completely cured;
whatever illnesses exist within the body, they are all treated and healed.
Neither yakṣas, rākṣasas, vināyakas, nor malevolent demons, ghosts,
or spirits can cause them harm; furthermore,
they shall have no fear of weapons, water, fire, evil winds, rain, hail, enemies, robbers, wicked kings, or bandits.
In the end, they will be unable to cause harm, nor will there be untimely death;
furthermore, there will be no evil dreams, nor venomous snakes, vipers, scorpions,
lizards, centipedes, spiders, or any other evils.
Poisonous beasts, lions, tigers, and wolves shall all be unable to harm them.
In military conflicts and battle arrays, they shall always achieve victory.
If there are official matters or legal disputes, they shall all be resolved through reconciliation.
If one recites this dhāraṇī once,
all such matters as those mentioned above will be fulfilled according to one's wishes.
If one recites this dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times every day, [the same shall occur].
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva saw them and addressed them, saying:
"O sons of good family, do not fear.
Whatever wish you seek, I shall grant it all to you."
Amitābha Buddha manifests his own body.
One sees the adornments of the Land of Ultimate Bliss as described in the sutras,
and also sees the assembly of bodhisattvas in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
They also see all the Buddhas of the ten directions and the Mount Potalaka where the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara dwells;
immediately, their own bodies become pure.
They will always be reverently honored and provided for by kings, dukes, high ministers, and counselors, and be loved and respected by all people.
In whatever place they are born, they will not dwell within a mother’s womb;
rather, they will be born upon lotus flowers, exquisitely adorned and sublime.
In whatever place they are born, they shall always possess the recollection of past lives.
From this day forth until they attain Buddhahood,
they shall never fall into the evil realms and shall always be born in the presence of the Buddhas.
Chapter Two: All Dharmas for Universal Delight. At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, out of compassion for sentient beings, [spoke].
Furthermore, the Secret Wish-Fulfilling Mind-Wheel Dhāraṇī is taught.
Whatever is required comes of its own accord; there are two kinds of wealth:
first, worldly wealth.
The second is supramundane wealth.
Mundane wealth refers to treasures such as gold and silver;
supramundane wealth consists of the two adornments of merit and wisdom.
With body and mind filled with joy, one is loved and respected by all;
able to rescue all sentient beings from suffering,
one’s heart of compassion increases and one can bestow wisdom upon others.
The various implements of pleasure and the necessities of life can augment one's power;
however, this realm of the secret treasury must not be spoken of to others.
If you wish to obtain this most supreme efficacy of the Cintāmaṇicakra Dhāraṇī, you should,
with a sincere heart, constantly recite and uphold it at all times and in all places,
whether in a state of purity or impurity.
First, ensure that there are no errors and that the recitation of the daily liturgy is complete;
furthermore, one should invoke the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and the Cintāmaṇicakra Dhāraṇī.
He shall also utter that person’s name,
or at times bring them to mind—
whether it be a king, a prince, a queen, a princess, a brahmin, a kṣatriya, a vaiśya, or a śūdra.
Whether they be men or women, boys or girls, or various followers of external paths,
if they merely wish to pay their respects, one should call out their names;
this should be done every time the fifth watch arrives so that the daily recitation may be fulfilled.
If one seeks the most excellent efficacy,
by personally attending upon a king for seven days and reciting [the mantra] one thousand and eight times at every fifth watch of the night, one will immediately obtain an audience with him.
If one wishes to see the queen or consort, one should recite nine hundred times;
if one wishes to see the prince, one should recite eight hundred times;
if one wishes to see the palace attendants, one should recite seven hundred times.
If one wishes to see a princess, recite it six hundred times.
If one wishes to have an audience with a Brahmin, recite it five hundred times.
If one wishes to have an audience with a Kṣatriya, recite it four hundred times.
Recite the Vaiśravaṇa mantra three hundred times;
for bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs, one hundred times;
and for upāsakas and upāsikās, ninety times.
Recite this sixty times for a boy or a girl;
this is called the method of the preliminary practice (*upacāra-vidhi*),
which is capable of accomplishing all matters.
Whatever wealth, slaves, horses, or all manner of enjoyments one desires,
even those sought from afar, shall arrive as swiftly as the wind.
For whatever task one wishes to perform, merely by completing the required recitation, that matter will be accomplished.
If one wishes to behold the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
by reciting [the name] one thousand and eight times,
one will immediately see his true body and all things will be fulfilled.
If one wishes to see Vajrapāṇi, one should recite [the mantra] ten thousand times;
he will then appear before that person, regard them with compassion as a father loves his son,
and grant all that the heart desires.
If one wishes to see the various Buddhas and their great assemblies,
one will see them immediately upon reciting [the mantra] thirteen thousand times.
If one recites it continuously for seven days and seven nights, they will likewise appear.
All the deities associated with the dhāraṇīs he maintains will appear before him;
each shall bestow their respective dhāraṇī powers upon that person and constantly follow, protect, and guard them.
On the seventh day, the Lord of the Trichiliocosm,
together with Śakra, King of Devas,
and all their retinues, came together and granted him his vows.
Those who are able to rely upon the method of recitation as previously described shall have all their aspirations fulfilled. Chapter Three:

The Method for the Āgada Medicine to Make Others Feel Affection and Joy. Regarding the third chapter, "The Method for the Āgada Medicine to Make Others Feel Affection and Joy" from the Avalokiteśvara Dhāraṇī, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, out of compassion for sentient beings, [spoke as follows].
The method for preparing the medicinal elixir of love and joy is now explained;
when those who see it give rise to a heart of gladness,
once the compounding is complete, one should wear it upon the body.
To achieve all supreme accomplishments and have every wish fulfilled: ox-gallstone, white sandalwood, saffron, camphor, storax, mung beans, clove, *kakkola*, lotus, blue lotus, and gold leaf.
Take equal portions of each;
mix the white honey with the medicine in equal parts and pound them together.
Recite the aforementioned mantra one thousand and eight times.
When using incense to fumigate the body or clothing,
or when applying it to the eyelids, dotting the forehead, or smearing the body—
at such times, if it is for a king, a queen, or a crown prince.
The hundred officials, palace attendants, men, and women all took delight in him;
they revered this Dharma and resolved to attain Bodhicitta.
They did not begrudge their physical strength or material wealth, offering it all as service and attendants for him, such that their deeds could not be fully described.
Just as the sun and moon are desired by all to behold and are able to accomplish every task, so too,
if a person wears or carries this medicine, their karmic obstacles and hindrances will be extinguished.
All calamities and hardships shall be completely liberated from;
whether by a king’s powerful seizure,
drowning in water, burning by fire, or various weapons and poisons.
All fetters and afflictions shall be liberated;
one need only apply oneself with a sincere heart.
However, this medicine must not be taken into the mouth recklessly.

4. Chapter Four: The Section on the Contained Substances of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel of Avalokiteśvara. Out of compassion for sentient beings, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara further taught the substances to be held in the mouth, which cause all to be filled with joy and affection.
Camphor, storax, and saffron should be finely ground and mixed with cow bezoar.
Recite each of the three aforementioned mantras one thousand and eight times,
then blend them with pure water.
Form them into pills the size of *wutong* seeds.
Recite each of the three mantras one hundred and eight times.
Dry them in the shade, ensuring they are not exposed to wind or sunlight.
For each of these pills, recite the three preceding mantras seven times each,
and then place one pill inside the mouth. This applies to kings,
ministers, the great assembly, and similar classes of people.
When speaking with even a single person, he immediately gives rise to a sense of reverence;
he does not begrudge his wealth and treasures,
but gives everything that anyone requires.
All that is spoken shall be believed and accepted by all;
whatever one prays for shall be entirely fulfilled.
When applying medicine to the mouth, one must constantly recite the mantra.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva will immediately grant their wish.
One should prepare a square altar before an image of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva using scented water, measuring four cubits in length and breadth.
Place various kinds of flowers within the mandala;
as for flowers from trees or grasses, simply seek out whatever can be obtained.
Burn white sandalwood incense and take the aforementioned pill medicine and place it within the mandala.
Erect four banners and spread a white canopy; suspend four white streamers above the altar.
Make offerings to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, and then recite the Heart Mantra and the Heart-of-the-Heart Mantra one hundred and eight times each.
Recite the body mantra one hundred and eight times, then scatter white sandalwood incense and flowers.
At that time, all requests for wishes shall be obtained.
Take the medicinal substances from within the mandala and wear them as an amulet.
In whatever place one goes, one shall obtain all that one seeks;
whatever one says shall be fully believed and accepted;
and all undertakings shall be successfully accomplished, except in cases where there is a lack of sincere devotion.
5. The Fifth Chapter on the Eye Medicine of the Mind-Cakra of Avalokiteśvara. At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, out of compassion for sentient beings, taught the method for eye medicine.

It causes all who see it to give rise to love, delight, and joy. [The ingredients are: māṃsī, kuṣṭha, red lotus, blue lotus, sea-foam, or the powder of cuttlefish bone, bovine bezoar, saffron, *hāny-kuṅkuma*, long pepper, black pepper, and ginger.
Having divided [the ingredients] equally and pounded them finely until sieved,
take one liang of the aforementioned medicine and add half a liang of *śrīkhaṇḍa* (sandalwood) and *karpūra* (camphor), grinding them finely.
Before the image of Avalokiteśvara,
combine [the ingredients] and recite each of the three preceding mantras one thousand and eight times.
Toward all sentient beings, give rise to a mind of loving-kindness and compassion.
Place this medicine beneath the feet of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. Then, upon touching it,
one may immediately take a copper wire,
apply the medicine to its tip, and place it at the corner of the eye.
It cures all diseases of the eyes,
including cataracts, white halos, tearing, red membranes, blindness, and headaches.
Apply this medicine once daily and place it within the eyes.
All eye diseases shall be cured.
On the second day, it cures all diseases within the body.
On the third day, it cures the eighty-four types of epilepsy.
On the fourth day, one wears it so that all internal and external obstacles cannot hinder them.
On the fifth day, one wears it so that in all battles with hostile enemies and armed forces, one attains victory.
On the sixth day, one wears it so that all evil karma and afflictions [are overcome].
It can utterly destroy the four grave offenses, the five heinous crimes, evil dreams, and malevolent sorcery;
one shall never fall into the three evil realms for seven days, and it shall reach the kings, ministers, and all the great assemblies.
All will accord with, revere, believe in, accept, and delight in [this].
If one is possessed by it for two weeks, one will attain great sovereignty.
If one is possessed by it for three weeks, one will be able to have close audiences with kings and ministers.
During the fourth seven-day period, all yakṣas along with their retinues shall serve as his attendants.
During the fifth seven-day period, asuras, nāgas, yakṣas, and rākṣasas shall all serve as his attendants.
After six or seven days, he will possess great power; flying rākṣasas,
those who practice spirit-possession, and practitioners of sorcery and bewitchment—
even until he attains Buddhahood— will constantly follow and protect him.
During the seventh seven-day period, he was possessed by the Mahākāla spirit and even the spirits of the eight classes;
they all came to follow him and serve as his attendants.
During the eighth seven-day period, he was possessed by various people who could not see him.

Upon wearing it for nine weeks, one will see all hidden treasures; upon wearing it for seventeen days, the gates of the asura palaces will open spontaneously, and one will see everything within the palaces, entering and exiting without obstruction.
On the eleventh week, all medicinal substances are applied;
like a blazing fire, they manifest as remedies for every ailment.
If one seeks long life or great power, these shall be attained.
In the twelfth week, the various mountains open up,
and precious objects appear, which may be taken and used at will.
In the thirteenth week, the dragon palaces spontaneously open, and precious objects appear.
Whatever he beholds is entirely without obstruction.
During the fourteenth week, there is no palace of the devas in the desire realm that he does not enter and see.
During the fifteenth week, even within the pitch-black darkness of night, it is as if it were broad daylight.
In the sixteenth week, one perceives the earth beneath the ground, the golden earth, the vajra earth, the water wheel, the wind wheel, and the space wheel.
In the seventeenth week, one perceives all sentient beings within the hells throughout the four continents.
By virtue of having already attained the vision of that power, all sentient beings suffering in pain obtain liberation.
During the eighteenth seven-day period, one is endowed with the power of that person’s merit like the sun.
During the nineteenth seven-day period, one attains the vision of the Vajra True Body, and all vows are fulfilled.
On the twenty-seventh day, one attains the vision of the Greatly Compassionate Avalokiteśvara, whereby all vows are fulfilled.
On the twenty-first seventh day (the fourteenth day), one soars through the void.
One sees that all the celestial palaces of the gods in the realm of form are wide open;
furthermore, one sees the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions, as well as their pure buddha-lands.
If one practices this for one year, one will attain five kinds of pure eyes.
Those who are able to cultivate this Dharma should have deep faith in this teaching.
Out of compassion for sentient beings, they must not give rise to doubt;
for the Dharma is difficult to accomplish, as has been explained above.

6. The Chapter on the Hòu-om Dhāraṇī. The sixth chapter, the Chapter on the Hòu-om Dhāraṇī of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, [is taught] because Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva has compassion for sentient beings.
I shall now explain the *Agnioṃkāra-śrī-dharma*,
which is capable of accomplishing all undertakings and destroying all afflictions, karmic obstructions, and evil deeds.
If there are enemies, they shall all be subdued.
Even if Vināyakas harbor a mind of malice, it will immediately cease of its own accord and no longer cause harm.
All people will develop love and respect for them.
Dig into the ground to construct a hearth, one cubit square.
Combine *mālī*, *mallikā*, white mustard seeds, curd, honey, and ghee in equal portions.
Use fuel sticks of agallochum (*agaru*) and sandalwood (*candana*), each twelve finger-widths long and measured across the width of a finger.
Cut it and place it in the furnace to burn.
Scoop up a small amount of the medicine with the hand,
recite the mantra once, and cast it into the fire to burn.
Reciting it thus one thousand and eight times will destroy all karmic obstructions and extend one’s lifespan to two hundred and twenty years.
By continuing for seven days, one can perform the *oṃ*-mantra rite.
With a lifespan of one thousand years, their bodies will be pure.

By performing the ritual for two weeks, kings, crown princes, ministers, commoners, and ordinary people will take refuge in them with reverence. By performing the ritual for three weeks, the Heaven of the Thirty-three and its retinue [will likewise be won over].
The Sun and Moon, the Four Heavenly Kings,
and their retinues all came to provide protection;
the Rakṣasas and Vajras brought about great efficacy.
If Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva fulfills his great vow such that a land suffers from a lack of rain,
one should take white mustard seeds and clarified butter and recite the mantra over them in succession for three days;
if these are then burned in a fire, rain will immediately fall.
If rain falls incessantly, take the ashes from this hearth and recite the mantra over them one hundred and eight times;
scatter them toward the four directions and above, and the rain will immediately cease. If malicious hail falls or a violent wind suddenly arises, [perform the same].
Furthermore, recite this ash-spell one hundred and eight times and scatter it from afar toward where clouds are gathering;
then cease. If one constantly recites this spell, its power will be like that of Nārāyaṇa.
After casting off this body, one will be reborn in the World of Ultimate Bliss (Sukhāvatī).
"In whatever place one is born, one shall always attain the recollection of past lives until the attainment of Buddhahood.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, this Candana-citta-cakra-dhāraṇī is as I have described it."
If any bhikṣu, bhikṣuṇī, upāsaka, or upāsikā—whether male or female—receives and maintains this, they will certainly achieve accomplishment; do not harbor any doubt.
Whatever matters one contemplates in the mind, all shall be attained.
"You must have profound faith and must not give rise to doubt.
At that time, the Buddha praised Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, Great Compassionate Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Mahāsattva!"
You are thus able to expound this subtle and wondrous *Cintāmaṇicakra-dhāraṇī* method,
which manifests in Jambudvīpa to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings;
if one arouses the mind and recites it orally, one shall immediately obtain its efficacious results.
Although you have followed my teaching and repeatedly exerted yourself with diligence to instruct all sentient beings,
thereby producing efficacious results and manifesting your own form.
"Do not disobey my words; I shall rejoice in them.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Buddha, saying, "World-Honored One, throughout immeasurable kalpas, I have, with a heart of compassion, received the entrustment of sentient beings, constantly providing protection and manifesting efficacious responses for them."
The Buddha, having personally realized it for the sake of sentient beings,
has taught this *Cintāmaṇicakra Dhāraṇī*.
If there are those who receive and uphold it, constantly performing their own recitations, all their aspirations shall be fulfilled.
"Relying upon the Buddha's power, I thus rescue sentient beings from suffering.
At that time, having spoken this *Sūtra of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel Dhāraṇī*, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara [concluded].
The entire great assembly was filled with immense joy; they believed, accepted, and practiced it.
*Avalokiteśvara-guhyakośa-cintāmaṇicakra-dhāraṇī-sūtra*. Namo ratnatrayāya. Namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya.
1. *Teṣāṃ* 2. *Vajraya* 3. *Buddhādhiṣṭhita-sattvaya* 4.
*Mahāsattvaya* 5. *Mahākāruṇika-ka* 6. *Tadyathā* 7. *Oṃ hūṃ* 8. *Cakra* (2)
Haketimati (8) Vidyotamāni (9) Mahāpradīpe (10) Ruruditeṣṭa (11) Jambhara (12) Aṅkuśaye (13) Hūṃ Phaṭ (short vowel). Sa.
VAṂ HA (the root body mantra). OṂ HŪṂ PADMĀMBHOJAMANIJA VAṂ RA HO HŪṂ (the aforementioned body mantra).
OṂ HŪṂ VARADĀYA PADME HO HŪṂ (the heart-to-heart mantra).
